chapter_note: The chapter contains a substantial correspondential-cosmological exposition (sunrise/sunset as revelations of the First Man’s descent and the Last Statue’s ascent). The opening and closing are hagiographic frame. A strong late drift occurs near the end: an explicit exhortation to preach/repentance (pastoral/application layer) follows a self-contained cosmological teaching sequence, consistent with the editorial-fatigue signal.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue-frame attribution (“Once again he speaks to his disciples…”) with imperative attention marker; typical redactional wrapper rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Two great mysteries are apparent in this shining sun, at its rising and setting. Now, at the moment when it rises and is visible in the universe, all creatures of flesh shall lift up their heads fr[om their sleep] towards the splendour of the sun, and open their doors. While at evening time, when the sun sinks from the universe, all people from every place and even all beasts shall go in to their dark hiding places. The population of the entire universe shuts their doors and dark night overcomes them. They go inside and stay within the dark night in their hiding places.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal correspondential setup using natural cycles (sunrise/sunset; opening/closing; day/night) as ‘mysteries’ without institutional address or citation; stays within cosmos/nature rather than pointing to contemporary practice.

paragraphs.core_text: Very great is this mystery revealed by the sun! For when the sun rises and [be]come[s] visible at the beginning of the day all people open their doors, and all of humanity and every creature emerges onto the ear[th] to destroy this Light Cross that is established i[n] silence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the mystery-language into a cosmological referent (“Light Cross”) and mythic action; still expository rather than exhortative.

paragraphs.core_text: This pertains to the mystery of the First Man, because when he came out from the grea[t]ness he shone forth over all the children of Darkness. At that mome[nt] all the children of Darkness came forth from their storehouses, its powers and its armies, abandoning their caves and their black abyss. They destroyed the [outer] body of his five sons, who were swathed over hi[s b]o[dy, in t]hat first struggle. ⟨p.165⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic mythic-cosmological explication (First Man; storehouses; powers/armies; five sons) in an impersonal explanatory voice; strong marker of the older teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, when the sun sinks from the universe and sets, and all people go in to their hiding places and houses and conceal themselves; this also pertains to the mystery of the end, as it presages the consummation of the universe. For, when all the light will be purified and redeemed i[n] the universe at the last, the collector of all things, the Last Statue, will gather in and sculpt it/self. It is the last hour of the day, the time when the Last Statue will go up to the aeo[n of] light. The enemy too, Death, will go in to bondage; to the prison of the souls of the de[ni]iers and blasphemers who loved the darkness. They will go in with it to bondage and the dark night overcomes th[em]; and thenceforth this name 'light' will not shine upon them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological completion of the correspondence (sunset → cosmic end) with internal cosmological agents (Last Statue; Death; bondage/prison mechanics). Though it includes moral labels (“deniers…blasphemers”), it remains description of cosmic sorting rather than institutional instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: Behold the two mysteries made visible daily in the sun, which is this splendrous light-giver.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding summary in the same expository register; closes the two-mystery teaching unit without shifting to church practice.

Direct audience address (“my brothers and loved ones”) + imperatives (train yourselves; preach) + repentance/time urgency: a clear pivot from cosmological exposition to community exhortation (late pastoral/application layer).
Narrativized reaction of disciples (“When his disciples heard…”) with emotive response and quoted plea; typical redactional scene-setting/closure rather than substrate exposition.
